cluster_summary: This cluster covers cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities arising from user-controlled data being inserted into the DOM via innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or markdown-to-HTML pipelines without proper sanitization or escaping. The root cause is the assumption that user input is safe for HTML context. Fix strategies range from using textContent or HTML encoding for plain text, adding DOMPurify or rehype-sanitize for HTML content, escaping attributes in custom renderers, to replacing dangerouslySetInnerHTML with JSX expressions or using DOM APIs with URL validation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 6 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add a sanitization step (rehype-sanitize, DOMPurify) after rendering, or escape attribute values (src, alt, title) in custom markdown renderers..
